snippets.text: In 1977, a rocket sent Voyager 2 on its way toward Jupiter.
snippets.spoken: In nineteen seventy-seven, a rocket sent Voyager 2 on its way toward Jupiter.

snippets.text: On its own, that launch wasn't enough to escape. Without Jupiter, its path would have curved back toward the Sun, never getting much farther out than Jupiter's distance.
snippets.spoken: On its own, that launch wasn't enough to escape. Without Jupiter, its path would have curved back toward the Sun, never getting much farther out than Jupiter's distance.

snippets.text: Instead, it bent at Jupiter. Then at Saturn. Then Uranus. Then Neptune.
snippets.spoken: Instead it bent at Jupiter. Then at Saturn. Then Uranus. Then Neptune.

snippets.text: Today, it's in interstellar space.
snippets.spoken: Today, it's in interstellar space.

snippets.text: So how can flying past a planet make a spacecraft faster? The answer depends on who's watching.
snippets.spoken: So how can flying past a planet make a spacecraft faster? The answer depends on who's watching.

snippets.text: Let's watch from the planet first. In this view, Jupiter sits still.
snippets.spoken: Let's watch from the planet first. In this view, Jupiter sits still.

snippets.text: Our spacecraft falls toward it, and speeds up as it drops in.
snippets.spoken: Our spacecraft falls toward it, and speeds up as it drops in.

snippets.text: It swings around, and starts climbing back out. And climbing out, it slows down again.
snippets.spoken: It swings around, and starts climbing back out. And climbing out, it slows down again.

snippets.text: By the time it's clear, with no engines firing, it's moving about as fast as when it arrived. Measured from Jupiter, the flyby gave it no extra speed.
snippets.spoken: By the time it's clear, with no engines firing, it's moving about as fast as when it arrived. Measured from Jupiter, the flyby gave it no extra speed.

snippets.text: But something did change. Look at the arrows. Same length. Different direction.
snippets.spoken: But something did change. Look at the arrows. Same length. Different direction.

snippets.text: That's the difference between speed and velocity. Speed is how fast. Velocity is how fast, and which way.
snippets.spoken: That's the difference between speed and velocity. Speed is how fast. Velocity is how fast, and which way.

snippets.text: The flyby left the speed alone. It turned the velocity.
snippets.spoken: The flyby left the speed alone. It turned the velocity.

snippets.text: Now let's watch the same flyby from the Sun. And here's what the first view hid: Jupiter isn't standing still. It's moving along its orbit.
snippets.spoken: Now let's watch the same flyby from the Sun. And here's what the first view hid: Jupiter isn't standing still. It's moving along its orbit.

snippets.text: The spacecraft still follows the same kind of curve around Jupiter. But now that curve is moving through space with the planet.
snippets.spoken: The spacecraft still follows the same kind of curve around Jupiter. But now that curve is moving through space with the planet.

snippets.text: Measured from Jupiter, the speed didn't change. Measured from the Sun, the spacecraft leaves faster than it arrived.
snippets.spoken: Measured from Jupiter, the speed didn't change. Measured from the Sun, the spacecraft leaves faster than it arrived.

snippets.text: Same flyby. Two answers. Both of them right.
snippets.spoken: Same flyby. Two answers. Both of them right.

snippets.text: Here's why. Seen from the Sun, the spacecraft's velocity is two arrows added together. Jupiter's motion, plus the spacecraft's motion relative to Jupiter.
snippets.spoken: Here's why. Seen from the Sun, the spacecraft's velocity is two arrows added together. Jupiter's motion, plus the spacecraft's motion relative to Jupiter.

snippets.text: During the flyby, Jupiter's arrow barely changes. The spacecraft's arrow keeps its length, but turns.
snippets.spoken: During the flyby, Jupiter's arrow barely changes. The spacecraft's arrow keeps its length, but turns.

snippets.text: Turned to point more along Jupiter's motion, the two arrows add up to a longer one. That longer arrow is the speed gain, measured from the Sun.
snippets.spoken: Turned to point more along Jupiter's motion, the two arrows add up to a longer one. That longer arrow is the speed gain, measured from the Sun.

snippets.text: So where does that extra energy come from? Not from nowhere.
snippets.spoken: So where does that extra energy come from? Not from nowhere.

snippets.text: The spacecraft's gravity pulls on Jupiter too. As the spacecraft gains orbital energy, Jupiter gives up a tiny amount of its own orbital energy.
snippets.spoken: The spacecraft's gravity pulls on Jupiter too. As the spacecraft gains orbital energy, Jupiter gives up a tiny amount of its own orbital energy.

snippets.text: Jupiter is so massive that the change is almost imperceptible. Its orbit carries on.
snippets.spoken: Jupiter is so massive that the change is almost imperceptible. Its orbit carries on.

snippets.text: The spacecraft didn't make speed. It borrowed it.
snippets.spoken: The spacecraft didn't make speed. It borrowed it.

snippets.text: Which way it turns decides everything.
snippets.spoken: Which way it turns decides everything.

snippets.text: Pass behind a moving planet, and you can leave faster, relative to the Sun.
snippets.spoken: Pass behind a moving planet, and you can leave faster, relative to the Sun.

snippets.text: Pass in front of it, and the turn works against you. You leave slower.
snippets.spoken: Pass in front of it, and the turn works against you. You leave slower.

snippets.text: So a flyby can be an accelerator, or a brake. Galileo skimmed past Jupiter's moon Io to shed energy, and saved ninety kilograms of fuel.
snippets.spoken: So a flyby can be an accelerator, or a brake. Galileo skimmed past Jupiter's moon Eyeo to shed energy, and saved ninety kilograms of fuel.

snippets.text: Now for the real thing. In the late nineteen-seventies, the four giant planets drifted into a favourable alignment, one that comes around roughly once every hundred and seventy-five years.
snippets.spoken: Now for the real thing. In the late nineteen-seventies, the four giant planets drifted into a favourable alignment, one that comes around roughly once every hundred and seventy-five years.

snippets.text: The alignment made a journey past all four possible. Voyager 2's trajectory kept that door open. And it took it.
snippets.spoken: The alignment made a journey past all four possible. Voyager Two's trajectory kept that door open. And it took it.

snippets.text: At Jupiter, its path bent toward Saturn. At Saturn, toward Uranus. At Uranus, toward Neptune, which it reached in nineteen eighty-nine.
snippets.spoken: At Jupiter, its path bent toward Saturn. At Saturn, toward Uranus. At Uranus, toward Neptune, which it reached in nineteen eighty-nine.

snippets.text: Its twin, Voyager 1, took a different road. A close pass by Saturn's moon Titan sent it away from any further giant-planet encounters.
snippets.spoken: Its twin, Voyager 1, took a different road. A close pass by Saturn's moon Titan sent it away from any further giant-planet encounters.

snippets.text: Measured from the Sun, those flybys more than doubled Voyager 2's speed. And that dashed path is where it would have gone without them.
snippets.spoken: Measured from the Sun, those flybys more than doubled Voyager Two's speed. And that dashed path is where it would have gone without them.

snippets.text: So if a planet can fling you out of the Solar System, falling into the Sun should be easy. It's just falling, after all.
snippets.spoken: So if a planet can fling you out of the Solar System, falling into the Sun should be easy. It's just falling, after all.

snippets.text: The catch: Earth is racing sideways around the Sun at about thirty kilometres a second. And so is everything we launch from it.
snippets.spoken: The catch: Earth is racing sideways around the Sun at about thirty kilometres a second. And so is everything we launch from it.

snippets.text: Aim straight at the Sun, and that sideways speed carries you right past it. To fall in, you have to get rid of it.
snippets.spoken: Aim straight at the Sun, and that sideways speed carries you right past it. To fall in, you have to get rid of it.

snippets.text: That was the problem facing NASA's Parker Solar Probe. It needed to shed about fifty-three thousand miles per hour of sideways speed.
snippets.spoken: That was the problem facing NASA's Parker Solar Probe. It needed to shed about fifty-three thousand miles per hour of sideways speed.

snippets.text: So it used the brake. It flew past Venus seven times.
snippets.spoken: So it used the brake. It flew past Venus seven times.

snippets.text: Taken together, those flybys reduced its orbital energy around the Sun, letting its orbit reach closer and closer in. The last one came in November twenty twenty-four.
snippets.spoken: Taken together, those flybys reduced its orbital energy around the Sun, letting its orbit reach closer and closer in. The last one came in November twenty twenty-four.

snippets.text: Here's the twist. With its orbital energy reduced, Parker fell deep toward the Sun. On Christmas Eve, twenty twenty-four, it passed about six million kilometres from the surface, faster than anything humans have built.
snippets.spoken: Here's the twist. With its orbital energy reduced, Parker fell deep toward the Sun. On Christmas Eve, twenty twenty-four, it passed about six million kilometres from the surface, faster than anything humans have built.

snippets.text: It got there by slowing down first.
snippets.spoken: It got there by slowing down first.

snippets.text: So here's the whole trick, in three parts. One: change your view. From the planet, a flyby only turns you. From the Sun, that turn can change your speed.
snippets.spoken: So here's the whole trick, in three parts. One: change your view. From the planet, a flyby only turns you. From the Sun, that turn can change your speed.

snippets.text: Two: nothing is created. Orbital energy is transferred between the spacecraft and the planet.
snippets.spoken: Two: nothing is created. Orbital energy is transferred between the spacecraft and the planet.

snippets.text: Three: aim decides. Relative to the Sun, pass behind, and you speed up. Pass in front, and you slow down.
snippets.spoken: Three: aim decides. Relative to the Sun, pass behind, and you speed up. Pass in front, and you slow down.

snippets.text: Voyager 1 is still heading out. On the eighteenth of November, twenty twenty-six, it crosses the one-light-day mark.
snippets.spoken: Voyager 1 is still heading out. On the eighteenth of November, twenty twenty-six, it crosses the one-light-day mark.

snippets.text: A message from home will take almost a day to reach it.
